title: Police fire tear gas at cost-of-living protesters in Lyon
seoTitle: Lyon protests over living costs and bans

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated over the high cost of living, school conditions, and strained public services.
tea.want: Better living conditions and government action on economic grievances.
tea.changed: Oct 24: Police used tear gas to disperse around 150 protesters in Lyon where gatherings were banned.

summary: On October 24, 2026, fresh demonstrations regarding the high cost of living and strained public services took place across France, including Lyon. In Lyon, where authorities had banned public demonstrations in parts of the city, police deployed tear gas to disperse a group of about 150 protesters near the city center after participants briefly attempted to block a road. Nationwide, tens of thousands participated in the rallies, which followed earlier unrest and looting. The government deployed 70,000 security personnel and implemented local curfews and demonstration bans, drawing criticism from unions, left-wing parties, and human rights groups such as Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch over restrictions on the right to protest.
demands: Address the high cost of living
response: According to sources, authorities deployed 70,000 security personnel nationwide, banned demonstrations in several cities including Lyon, and police used tear gas to disperse protesters.
